requirements.evidence: Members.php:113-136 makes openMember/saveRole/confirmRemoval/cancelRemoval/removeMember empty stubs; PendingInvites.php:35 writes `'user_id' => $invite->email`; PendingInvites.php:46 returns redirect() from a `void` method; EntityInviteMail.php:6 imports a non-existent `Illuminate\Foundation\Mailable` and has no ShouldQueue/content(); resources/views/emails/entity-invite.blade.php:2-12 uses keys that exist in no lang file; no members view, no pending-invites view, no switcher/onboarding integration, no lang/pt_BR.json entry. Requirements 1 (email normalisation), 3 (role validation), 5, 6 and the whole members-page section are missing or broken.

conventions.evidence: Uses the project's `#[Validate]`/`#[Fillable]` attributes and a reversible migration, but: inviteRole has no `#[Validate]`, invite acceptance/invite writes bypass an app/Actions use case (Members.php:38-99, PendingInvites.php:19-47), policies for `accept`/`decline`/`delete` on EntityInvite are absent, the migration file name has no HHMMSS component (2026_10_29_create_entity_invites_table.php), and no CHANGELOG/docs/tests are updated.

security.evidence: PendingInvites.php:62-66 lists every invite for the entity with no e-mail filter, disclosing other users' invite addresses; PendingInvites.php:12 exposes `$entityId` as an unlocked client-writable property; Members.php:28 leaves `inviteRole` unvalidated while treating it as client input; Members.php:34-36 mount never authorizes owner/admin; accept/decline trust non-existent policy methods instead of the required invitee e-mail check (PendingInvites.php:22,52).

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no test files at all (ends at resources/views/emails/entity-invite.blade.php:13); no happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or tamper tests for sendInvite, cancelInvite, openMember, saveRole, removeMember, accept or decline.

We need to find or create user by email` (PendingInvites.php:35), plus inconsistent parameter names (`$id` vs `$inviteId` in PendingInvites.php:19-20) make it hard to tell finished code from placeholders.

scope.evidence: Most of the diff serves the task, but app/Models/Entity.php:37 removes the `HasMany` return type from `memberships()` (an unrelated regression) and imports EntityInvite from its own namespace; no unrelated features were added.

issues.explanation: openMember(), saveRole(), confirmRemoval(), cancelRemoval() and removeMember() are empty stubs, so the member detail modal, role saving, removal confirmation and removal itself are not implemented at all.
Accepting creates a membership with `'user_id' => $invite->email`, writing an e-mail string into a user foreign key instead of resolving the signed-in user, so acceptance cannot succeed.
`accept(int $inviteId): void` returns `redirect()->route(...)`, which is a PHP fatal error (a void function must not return a value).

It imports `Illuminate\Foundation\Mailable`, which does not exist (the class is `Illuminate\Mail\Mailable`), does not implement ShouldQueue, and has no `content()` returning markdown `emails.entity-invite`, breaking the required mailable contract.
The file imports the `HasFactory` attribute class and then uses it as a trait (`use HasFactory;`), which is a fatal error and prevents `EntityInvite::factory()` from working.
`return \\App\\Models\\Entity::factory()->create()->id;` contains doubled backslashes, which is a PHP parse error; the factory file cannot load.

Every string comes from `emails.entity-invite.*` keys that are never added to any lang file, so the required greeting, instruction, button, expiry and signature text (and their pt_BR translations) will render as raw keys.

`inviteRole` has no `#[Validate]` rule, so `$this->validate()` never returns it and the role expression always falls back to `employee`; an admin role can never be invited, and invalid roles are silently coerced instead of rejected.
`mount()` only assigns the entity and never authorizes owner/admin, so employees are not denied with 403 on the Livewire component.

The members Blade view, the `livewire.entity.pending-invites` view, the entity-switcher/onboarding embedding and all new lang keys are absent from the diff, so none of the new UI (invite form, pending list, modals, titles, hr separation) exists.
The model does not normalise `email` to lowercase/trim on write, as requirement 1 explicitly demands so that every write path agrees.

The list query filters only by entity, not by the signed-in user's e-mail (case-insensitively), leaking other users' invite addresses and violating the requirement that only the invitee sees their invites.

`$entityId` is a public, unlocked property, so a client can point the component at another entity's invites; there is also no e-mail-match check before accept (it relies on policy abilities that are not defined anywhere in the diff).
No Pest/PHPUnit tests are included for any new behaviour, and the conventions require happy-path, validation-failure, unauthorized-call and tamper tests for every Livewire action.

The rate limiter is hit before the duplicate-member and pending-invite checks, so rejected attempts consume the quota even though only successful invites should count, and exhaustion aborts with 429 rather than a form error.

The unique-violation handler keys off MySQL-specific `errorInfo[1] === 1062`, so on SQLite (the test driver) or other databases the exception is rethrown and becomes a 500 instead of an `inviteEmail` error.
The migration filename lacks the HHMMSS time component produced by `php artisan make:migration`, so the file was not generated as the conventions require.

The change introduces a table and domain behaviour but does not update `CHANGELOG.md` (under `[Unreleased]`) or `docs/business-rules.md`/`docs/database-schema.md` as the docs-in-sync convention requires.
The unrelated change drops the `HasMany` return type from `memberships()` (and adds a redundant same-namespace import), a regression outside the task.
`ASSIGNABLE_ROLES` is now unused dead code left behind after removing `assignRole()`.

review.summary: The change sketches invite storage, a mailable, a pending-invites component and a partial Members rewrite, but it cannot run: it has fatal PHP errors (wrong Mailable namespace, HasFactory attribute used as a trait, doubled backslashes, returning a value from a void method), empty stubs for all member-management actions, no views or lang files, and no tests. Requirements coverage is minimal and there are concrete security gaps (unfiltered invite listing, unlocked entityId, unvalidated inviteRole), so the pull request must be rejected.
